slides.title: What is Economics?
slides.text:
What is Economics?
Economics is the study of the nature and causes of the wealth of nations
Adam Smith (1776)
Economics is a study of man in the ordinary business of life; it examines that part of individual and social action which is most closely connected with the attainment and use of the material requisites of well-being.
Alfred Marshall (1890)
Economics is the science which studies human behaviour as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses.
Lionel Robbins (1932)
Economics is the study of how societies use scarce resources to produce valuable commodities and distribute them among different people, examined across time and often employing insights from history.
Paul Samuelson (1948)

slides.title: Managerial Economics
slides.text:
Managerial Economics
Study of how to direct scarce resources in the way that most efficiently achieves a managerial goal
Examples:
What price should a firm charge for its product?
How much output should be produced?
How many workers should be hired?
Microeconomics vs Macroeconomics
Managerial economics leans heavily towards microeconomics

slides.title: Different types of costs
slides.text:
Different types of costs
Accounting Costs
The explicit costs of the resources needed to produce produce goods or services.
Reported on the firm’s income statement.
Examples: wages, rent, electricity, raw materials
Opportunity Cost
The cost of the explicit and implicit resources that are foregone when a decision is made.
Examples: owner's time, foregone salary, own building used for business
Economic Profits
Total revenue minus total opportunity cost.
Provides a complete measure of profitability

slides.title: Understanding Incentives
slides.text:
Understanding Incentives
Managers use incentives to encourage employees to work toward organizational goals.
Example: Sales Representative
Firm's goal: Increase sales.
Employee's incentive: Earn a sales commission.
Result: Higher effort → Higher sales → Higher earnings for the employee and higher profits for the firm.
Effective managers design incentives that align employees' interests with organizational goals.

slides.title: Understand Market dynamics
slides.text:
Understand Market dynamics
Markets involve interactions among different participants
Consumers vs. Producers
Competition Among Consumers for scarce goods and services, especially when demand exceeds supply.
Competition Among Producers for customers
Governments influence markets through laws, taxes, subsidies, and regulations.
Market Structure Matters: Firm behaviour and profitability depend on the type of market in which they operate.
Managers must understand how consumers, competitors, and government policies shape the market environment.

slides.title: Understand time value of money
slides.text:
Understand time value of money
Business decisions are long horizon, the value of money today will differ from tomorrow.
Would you prefer ₹10,000 today or ₹10,000 one year from now? Why?
The opportunity cost of receiving ₹10,000 one year from now is the amount of interest foregone that could be earned from investing ₹10,000 today.

Time value of money
The present value (PV) reflects the difference between the future value and the
opportunity cost of waiting (OCW).
Succinctly, PV = FV – OCW
If i = 0, note PV = FV.
As ‘i’ increases, the higher is the OCW and the lower the PV.

slides.title: Marginal Principle
slides.text:
Marginal Principle
To maximize net benefits, the managerial control variable should be increased up to the point where MB = MC.
MB > MC means the last unit of the control variable increased benefits more than it increased costs.
MB < MC means the last unit of the control variable increased costs more than it increased benefits.

slides.title: Conclusion
slides.text:
Conclusion
Make sure you include all costs and benefits when making decisions (opportunity cost).
When decisions span time, make sure you are comparing apples to apples (PV analysis).
Optimal economic decisions are made at the margin (marginal analysis).
